text:
Trump and Meloni continued their feud that was sparked during hte G7 summit(Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Italy's prime minister escalated a very public dispute with Donald Trump on Saturday after tensions mounted over claims that she had pleaded with the president for a photo opportunity at the G7 summit.

Giorgia Meloni took to Instagram to post a direct response to a Truth Social post by Trump, branding his "unprovoked attacks" as "senseless."

Trump's post alleged that the prime minister requested "over and over again" to be photographed with him during the summit, citing her declining popularity back home.

"Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni asked, over and over, for a picture with me during the G-7 meeting in France," Trump wrote on Saturday. "She is doing poorly in Italy with her level of popularity, possibly because she turned down the United States of America, a Country that truly loves and protects Italy, when it came to denying Iran from obtaining or developing a Nuclear Weapon."

"Now, after the United States defeated Iran militarily, she wants to be friends again in order to get her “numbers up.” No thanks!!!" he continued.

Meloni's response to Trump

In her post, the right-wing leader fired back, stating that her popularity "depends on my ability to defend Italy's national interest."

"That is also what I did regarding the American military bases in Italy. Their use is governed by agreements that we have always respected, and that cannot be violated as long as I am Prime Minister. Italy remains a sovereign nation," she wrote.

She added that her friendship with the president "certainly has not helped" her popularity in Italy.

Meloni said her friendship with Trump has not helped her in Italy

The prime minister previously took a more diplomatic tone after Trump was interviewed by Italian press and said: "She begged me to take a picture with her. She wanted a picture with me so badly. I wouldn't have taken it, but I felt sorry for her."

Meloni said she was "astonished" and asserted the account by the president was "made up."

"Donald Trump's statements are completely made up. I am frankly astonished," she said in a statement. "I don't ‌know why ⁠the president of the United States behaves like this toward his allies: it is not the first time, moreover."

In retaliation for Trump's statements, Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said he was canceling a trip to the U.S. next week.

"The serious and offensive words of President Trump towards Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni offend all of Italy," Tajani wrote on X.

"For this reason, I have decided to cancel my visit to the United States scheduled for the next 21 and 22 June," he added.
